messages.author: 9e72ef8d095655b8
messages.subject: Re: Error when opening .csv file and running GGIR
parts:
Hey there

The csv file you uploaded contains data aggregated to 1 min epochs. I assume this is responsible for the error as GGIR by default works with 5s epochs. Do you have the raw data available with the original sampling frequency in .csv or .gt3x format?

Also, when working with csv files from actilife, have a look at the issue of exporting .csv files with time stamps from actilife in the following: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html

Hope this helps.

Cheers

Fabian

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error when opening .csv file and running GGIR
parts:
Hi pballester,

First step is to check whether you have the raw gt3x files. If yes then use those and stop using the csv files because they represent information generated by proprietary software and with critical information lost in the process.

If the csv file is the only thing you have then see documentation for GGIR argument dataFormat.
GGIR by default works with 5s epochs
This does not mean you cannot work with 1 minute epoch data, just change GGIR argument windowsizes, see documentation.

Also, when working with csv files from actilife, have a look at the issue of exporting .csv files with time stamps from actilife in the following: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html

ActiGraph csv files with high resolution data should be automatically recognised, so I am not sure it is necessary to work with read.myacc.csv. I think this needs to be removed from the tutorial.

Best,
Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error when opening .csv file and running GGIR
parts:
Hi Dr. Schwendinger,
I've got a snag with my Actigraph .csv file, similar to what Navarro faced. The error I'm getting is:

Error in g.part1(datadir = datadir, metadatadir = metadatadir, f0 = f0, : No files to analyse. Check that there are accelerometer files in the directory specified with argument datadir
Do I need to use the read.myacc.csv function for Actigraph .csv files, or should I follow the approach you suggested in response to Navarro?

Please use the gt3x files and do not use read.myacc.csv for Actigraph data.
Your error message indicates that you did not specify the datadir correctly because it cannot find the raw accelerometer files or you have files in your data directory that are not files that GGIR can process. If you are using csv files with count data then see documentation for GGIR argument dataFormat. However, if you have gt3x data then use that instead. We only facilitate ActiGraph csv files with aggregated (count) data for those researchers who still have old ActiGraph count data. For new studies I strongly advise against working with count data as that is really bad science: not transparent and significant information loss.

Best,
Vincent
